title: VIPcell prioritizes immune regulators associated with cardiac recovery in mouse heart failure
summary: VIPcell combined learned partial-least-squares models and causal-graph inference with single-nucleus data to prioritize immune regulators associated with response to neonatal stromal cells or their secretome in mouse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. The study measured treatment-associated functional improvement in two mouse models, cardiac regulatory-T-cell expansion, and loss of functional benefit after fingolimod treatment. Fingolimod sequesters lymphocytes broadly; these experiments support immune involvement without uniquely establishing a Treg-specific mechanism or individual predicted genes as causal. Modeling used four sequencing datasets with synthetic augmentation and internal cross-validation, not independent biological replication. Results are preclinical. This entry represents the January 2026 preprint; the later journal DOI is the same study, with online date and final-version changes unassessed.
ai_technology: VIPcell machine-learning framework (data augmentation, partial least-squares regression and causal-structure inference)
organization: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago; Northwestern University; Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University; University of Macau; Stony Brook University; University of Maryland; University of Nevada Las Vegas

evidence.tested: Treatment outcomes in two mouse models; immune-cell measurements and fingolimod perturbation within the discovery study.
evidence.unknown: No human efficacy or independent-team confirmation. Four sequencing datasets with synthetic augmentation do not provide independent replication. Fingolimod affects lymphocyte trafficking broadly, limiting Treg-specific causal interpretation. Later journal full-text changes not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: VIPcell learned PLS associations to cardiac E/e′ values and used DAS causal-graph inference to prioritize regulator hypotheses; subsequent experiments tested immune involvement, not every predicted causal edge.
